prompt: What is the practical difference between disabling a workflow and deleting its file?
explanation: Disabling is the pause button: the documented way to stop a workflow without deleting the file from the repository, and Enable brings it straight back. Deleting is the permanent route — you would restore it from git history, not from a button.

options.text: Deleting erases the workflow’s past runs along with the file
Disabling stops the triggers while keeping the file — one click re-enables it later
They are the same action under two names
Disabling also removes the workflow from the Actions tab
